"Although Harappa was the first site to be discovered, it was badly destroyed by brick-robbers. As early as 1875, Alexander Cunningham, the first Director-General of the Archaeological Survey of India (ASI), often called the father of Indian archaeology, noted that the amount of brick taken from the ancient site was enough to lay brick for 'about 100 miles' of the railway line between Lahore and Multan. Many of the ancient structures at the site were damaged. In contrast, Mohenjodaro was far better preserved. Cunningham, when excavating, found an ancient seal that was given to him. He tried to place it within the time-frame of the sixth century BCE to fourth century CE, the period of the earliest cities he was familiar with from Chinese pilgrim accounts, and thus missed the true antiquity of the Indus Valley."

"Although Harappa was the first site to be discovered, it was badly destroyed by brick-robbers. As early as 1875, Alexander Cunningham, the first Director-General of the Archaeological Survey of India (ASI), often called the father of Indian archaeology, noted that the amount of brick taken from the ancient site was enough to lay brick for 'about 100 miles' of the railway line between Lahore and Multan. Many of the ancient structures at the site were damaged. In contrast, Mohenjodaro was far better preserved. Cunningham, when excavating, found an ancient seal that was given to him. He tried to place it within the time-frame of the sixth century BCE to fourth century CE, the period of the earliest cities he was familiar with from Chinese pilgrim accounts, and thus missed the true antiquity of the Indus Valley."

What distinguished title is commonly accorded to Alexander Cunningham in the history of Indian archaeology?

options.text: The Pioneer of Radiocarbon Dating
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Inverts the governing property or boundary condition.

options.text: The Father of Indian Archaeology
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Accurately identifies the verified NCERT principle for The Plight of Harappa.

options.text: The Decipherer of the Harappan Script
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Applies an adjacent or reciprocal mathematical relation.

options.text: The Architect of New Delhi
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses related NCERT concepts or attributes.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
According to NCERT principles for Harappan Civilisation and Archaeology (Bricks, Beads and Bones) (The Plight of Harappa):
The Father of Indian Archaeology

Detailed Analysis:
1. Alexander Cunningham was the first Director-General of the Archaeological Survey of India (ASI) and is celebrated as the Father of Indian Archaeology.
Therefore, option (B) is the correct answer.

questionText:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Agricultural Developments):
(A) Terracotta Models of the Plough
(B) Ploughed Field
(C) Traces of Canals
(D) Water Reservoirs

List-II (Sites):
(I) Kalibangan
(II) Dholavira
(III) Cholistan
(IV) Shortughai

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Inverts the governing property or boundary condition.
Correct answer. Correctly maps each entity across columns.
Incorrect option. Applies an adjacent or reciprocal mathematical relation.
Incorrect option. Confuses related NCERT concepts or attributes.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
Matching agricultural features with archaeological sites:
- (A) Terracotta models of the plough: Found at sites in Cholistan and at Banawali (Haryana) -> (III).
- (B) Ploughed field with furrows: Discovered at Kalibangan (Rajasthan) -> (I).
- (C) Traces of canals: Unearthed at Shortughai in Afghanistan -> (IV).
- (D) Water reservoirs: Found cut into rock at Dholavira in Gujarat -> (II).
Thus, (A)-(III), (B)-(I), (C)-(IV), (D)-(II).
Hence, option (B) is the correct match.

questionText:
Arrange the major developments in Harappan Archaeology in a chronological order:

(A) Report of Alexander Cunningham on Harappan seal.
(B) S.R. Rao begins excavations at Lothal.
(C) Daya Ram Sahni begins excavations at Harappa.
(D) Vasant Shinde begins archaeogenetic research at Rakhigarhi.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Inverts the governing property or boundary condition.
Incorrect option. Applies an adjacent or reciprocal mathematical relation.
Incorrect option. Confuses related NCERT concepts or attributes.
Correct answer. Accurately identifies the chronological/logical progression.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
Milestones in Harappan archaeology: (A) Alexander Cunningham published his report on a Harappan seal in 1875; (C) Daya Ram Sahni began excavations at Harappa in 1921; (B) S.R. Rao began excavations at the port site of Lothal in 1955; (D) Prof. Vasant Shinde launched modern ancient DNA and archaeogenetic research at Rakhigarhi around 2015. Sequence: (A), (C), (B), (D).
Hence, option (D) is correct.
